key_insight: A physics-informed neural network can use motion time series to infer both the state and hydrodynamic coefficients in the Cummins equations for floating offshore structures.
engineering_relevance: This enables data-driven identification of added mass, damping, and hydrostatic restoring terms from observed dynamics, which is useful for offshore design, monitoring, and model updating.
method: Embed the Cummins equations as physics constraints in a PINN.
Estimate translational and rotational states from movement data.
Solve the inverse problem to recover hydrodynamic coefficients such as added mass and damping.
evidence_signal: The method was verified on free-decay cases for a sphere and a box, showing accurate state and coefficient estimation when sufficient motion data were available.
watch_item: Estimation accuracy depends strongly on the volume and quality of the motion data, so sparse or noisy measurements may reduce reliability.
paper_title: Estimating Hydrodynamic Coefficients for Floating Offshore Structures from Movement Data Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
